transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Avery Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Samir Rao (Velora Head of Platform), Lina Ortiz (Velora ML Eng), Tom Hsu (Velora Security), Priya Nambiar (Velora DevOps)

Quick summary (auto):
- Onboarding progress mostly complete; service account + secrets outstanding.
- Need VPC peering window and KMS key config for private deployment test.
- SE will run two benchmark profiles and share results; security to review SOC2/KMS notes.
- Next meeting: architecture deep-dive for security and networking.

Topics: onboarding checklist, VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration, bench results plan, latency vs throughput tuning, fallback routing, timeline and next steps

Action items (recapped in transcript): Avery to run benchmarks; Jordan to send pricing and docs; Velora to share CIDR and sample prompts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Alright thanks everyone for joining, good to see you all. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Samir Rao: Samir here, Lina, Tom and Priya also on our side.
[00:10] Lina Ortiz: hey all.
[00:12] Jordan Kim: Great. We've got Avery and Maya from Redwood - we'll go through onboarding checklist and then bench plan, and leave time for Tom's security questions.
[00:22] Avery Singh: Cool, I can kick us off with the infra status. From the last meet we provisioned the sandbox gateway and gave you the service account with minimal scopes; looks like there was an issue with the key rotation policy when Velora tried to attach the KMS key?
[00:35] Priya Nambiar: Yeah we attempted to attach but got a permission denied on the KMS role - we're double-checking our IAM roles. Also for the VPC peering we need to lock the maintenance window. We're proposing 12/15 02:00-05:00 UTC.
[00:48] Jordan Kim: That window should work from our side, but we'll validate in the next 24 hours. Samir, is that acceptable?
[00:55] Samir Rao: sounds ok, we just need to coordinate with our on-call.
[00:58] Maya Patel: We'll put the peering ops runbook in the shared drive.
[01:05] Tom Hsu: Before we do peering, can we get the SOC2 artifact set and any notes about KMS integration? Our security audit needs to see key wrap examples and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys or only envelope encryption.
[01:20] Jordan Kim: Sure — to be clear, for the private pilot we support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS/HSM; envelope encryption is the default but you can bring your own CMK for key wrapping. We'll send the SOC2 pack and an integration note with example KMS policies.
[01:34] Tom Hsu: Okay, please include sample policy JSON. Last time some of the names in docs were slightly off — saw "Redwood Private" spelled with variant — so just want the canonical doc for auditors.
[01:45] Avery Singh: Noted, we'll attach canonical artifacts. On the benchmark side, Lina and Samir, can you confirm the expected latency targets and typical payload sizes so we pick the right profile?
[01:56] Lina Ortiz: Our 95th perc target is 200ms end-to-end for short chat prompts (~50 tokens) for the clinical triage microservice. We also want a throughput test for bulk inference ~2k qps for batch summarization jobs — those can be larger, like 512 tokens.
[02:12] Avery Singh: Good — we'll run two tests: a low-latency chat profile (50 tokens, p95 goal 200ms) and a throughput profile (512 tokens, target 2k qps). We'll run them against the hosted variant and the dedicated reserved pool mimic.
[02:27] Samir Rao: Quick question — when you say "dedicated mimic" is that using your Dedicated product or just a config that approximates dedicated hardware? We want to understand how results map to our expected commit.
[02:38] Avery Singh: Right, good point — for the pilot we'll allocate a dedicated GPU pool in our staging cluster; it's not a production reserved contract but it uses the same runtime and quantization profile so results should map well. We'll annotate differences in the reporting.
[02:49] Jordan Kim: Also want to flag the caching and prefix KV settings — if your client implements prefix reuse we can show big gains in tokens-per-dollar. Lina, do you expect prefix reuse?
[03:00] Lina Ortiz: For triage chat yes, we have a fair amount of shared context so caching will help. For bulk summarization less so.
[03:07] Priya Nambiar: Network-wise, for the private deployment we plan to peer and route all inference egress through an internal NAT — is there any issue with large payloads and the gateway? We saw earlier that the gateway has a 2MB payload limit in some configs.
[03:21] Avery Singh: There is a configurable payload limit; default is 2MB but we can bump to 10MB for your staging env. Will need a config change and a quick restart window.
[03:30] Tom Hsu: On audit logging — are token-level logs available or is it only metadata? We need to ensure PHI isn't logged; also would prefer redaction hooks.
[03:41] Jordan Kim: By default we capture metadata and request hashes; raw prompt text can be redacted. For Private, we support full audit log retention but you control retention period and redact hooks via a webhook. We'll include that in the security doc.
[03:56] Samir Rao: Ok — that aligns with our compliance team. One more: SSO and RBAC — we need SAML+SCIM integration for provisioning service accounts and role mappings.
[04:06] Maya Patel: We have SAML and SCIM support. Jordan will send the onboarding checklist for SSO; we also have a short playbook for mapping entitlements to Redwood roles (admin, ops, viewer).
[04:18] Jordan Kim: I'll send that checklist with the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints.
[04:22] Lina Ortiz: Great. Back to benchmarks — Avery, what's your run cadence and how will you present results? CSV? Grafana?
[04:29] Avery Singh: We'll do raw CSV plus a summarized sheet with p50/p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and a Grafana link for request traces. We'll also include a column for config (quantization level, kv cache enabled/disabled).
[04:42] Priya Nambiar: Please make sure timestamps are in UTC — our ops folks hate timezone conversions.
[04:46] Avery Singh: Noted.
[04:48] Samir Rao: Also, if possible, include a short section on fallbacks — what happens if the dedicated pool is saturated and we want a graceful degrade to a cheaper model?
[04:58] Jordan Kim: Yep, we support routing policies. You can set a policy to fallback by latency or cost— e.g., if p95 > 350ms for 3 consecutive minutes, route to a lower-cost compatible variant. We'll propose a policy template.
[05:12] Tom Hsu: Do fallbacks maintain the same tokenization and model family? Concerned about hallucination differences.
[05:20] Avery Singh: They should be model-compatible variants; we also provide eval comparisons for hallucination metrics between variants. We'll include the hallucination delta in the bench report.
[05:33] Lina Ortiz: On hallucinations — we'll send a 1000-sample prompt set (de-identified) for you to run through the candidate models so we can see regression.
[05:41] Jordan Kim: Perfect, please share the file in the shared drive.
[05:44] Samir Rao: One operational question — token accounting: is it per request or per token returned? Need detail for cost forecasting.
[05:51] Maya Patel: It's per input+output token; the billing docs break down unit economics. Jordan will attach examples for your cost model.
[05:59] Jordan Kim: I'll also run a small cost simulation for your two workloads and include it with pricing.
[06:04] Priya Nambiar: For the peering run, can you confirm IP ranges Redwood uses on the staging cluster? We'll need to allow them on our firewall.
[06:12] Avery Singh: I'll include the staging CIDR. For the dedicated mimic we'll provision ephemeral IPs for the duration of the test — we'll list them in the runbook.
[06:23] Tom Hsu: Security nit — can you confirm whether HSM-backed keys are single-tenant or multi-tenant? Auditors ask.
[06:31] Jordan Kim: HSM can be customer-dedicated when requested as part of an enterprise Private deployment; for hosted pilot it's multi-tenant but wrapped with CMKs. We'll clarify in doc.
[06:45] Samir Rao: Good. Any open technical risks we should call out?
[06:48] Avery Singh: One is KV cache warm-up for the chat profile — initial requests may see cold p95 spikes. We'll run a warm-up run and include warm vs steady-state figures. Also, network jitter in peering can add tail latency; recommend during maintenance window we run repeat tests.
[07:03] Lina Ortiz: That's expected. We'll schedule the bench window right after peering so we test the fully-configured path.
[07:09] Jordan Kim: Ok, let me recap next steps before we run out of time.
[07:12] Jordan Kim: Action items: Avery will run the two benchmarks (low-latency and high-throughput) and post raw CSVs and summary by 12/17. Jordan to send SOC2/KMS integration docs, pricing, and SSO checklist by 12/13. Samir to confirm VPC peering window and send CIDR by 12/14. Lina to share de-identified prompt set by 12/14. We'll schedule a security and network deep-dive for the week of 12/20.
[07:34] Samir Rao: Sounds good. One quick ask — can we get an itemized table of what's included in the dedicated mimic so procurement can correlate to budget line items?
[07:44] Jordan Kim: Yes I'll include a short appendix with included CPU/RAM/GPUs and estimated hourly burn.
[07:50] Maya Patel: I'll also open a pilot ticket in our tracker and assign the items so we have end-to-end visibility.
[07:56] Priya Nambiar: Thanks, that helps.
[07:58] Tom Hsu: Quick final: please don't include any real PHI in the prompts you run for the bench; we've got to keep it de-id'd.
[08:06] Lina Ortiz: Confirmed, all prompts will be de-identified.
[08:09] Jordan Kim: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via the shared folder and email with the artifacts. If there's nothing else we'll adjourn.
[08:16] Samir Rao: No further questions. Thanks.
[08:18] Meeting end.

Post-meeting notes (auto):
- Bench plan: two profiles (chat low-latency 50 tokens p95 200ms; throughput 512 tokens 2k qps).
- Security: provide SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration sample policies, clarify HSM tenancy.
- Ops: confirm peering window 12/15-12/16, staging CIDR to be provided by customer.
- Schedule: security/network deep-dive week of 12/20.

References mentioned: shared drive link (placeholder): https://redwood.share/velora/pilot-artifacts , bench spreadsheet placeholder: https://redwood.tools/bench/CRM-98721/report

End of transcript.
